topic: Little Diomede (USA, ~80 residents) and Big Diomede (Russia, no civilians since 1948) lie about 3.8 km apart in the Bering Strait with the International Date Line between them; Alaska (UTC−9) and Chukotka (UTC+12) differ by 21 hours.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: You can see Russia from mainland Alaska on a clear day.
myths.reality: From Little Diomede you can see Big Diomede 3.8 km away; the Russian mainland is visible only from the islands or high ground on the Seward Peninsula in exceptional conditions.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Diomede Shorts are trivia voiceovers over a stock photo; nobody draws the Date Line down the strait on the satellite map, measures the 3.8 km gap to scale, and shows who is actually on each island.

existing.title: Can you see Russia from Alaska?

nasa_eo.title: Yesterday and Tomorrow Islands
nasa_eo.notes: Big Diomede (Russia) and Little Diomede (USA) are about 3.8 km apart; the International Date Line runs between them, so Big Diomede is almost a day ahead; Big Diomede's residents were relocated to the mainland in 1948.

arctic_portal.title: Diomede Islands
arctic_portal.notes: Little Diomede village has about 77 residents (2023); Big Diomede hosts only a Russian border guard post and weather station; 21-hour time difference across the strait.

wiki_diomede.title: Diomede Islands
wiki_diomede.notes: Islands 3.8 km apart; IDL between them; Big Diomede uninhabited since 1948 relocation; Little Diomede population 77 (2023).

timeanddate.title: Time zones: Alaska (AKST, UTC−9) and Anadyr (UTC+12)
timeanddate.notes: Anadyr/Chukotka is UTC+12 year-round; Alaska standard time is UTC−9: a 21-hour difference in winter.

noaa_dateline.title: Where is the International Date Line?
noaa_dateline.notes: The International Date Line passes through the Bering Strait between the Diomede Islands.

claims.text: Little Diomede (USA) and Big Diomede (Russia) are about 3.8 km apart in the Bering Strait.
vo: this is little diomede, an american village in the bering strait. that is big diomede, russian territory, just 3.8 kilometres away
from this beach, you can look across the water and see tomorrow
two islands, one short row apart, and tomorrow is always on the other side of the water
across water you could row in an hour
screen: The island where you can see tomorrow

claims.text: The International Date Line runs between the two islands; Alaska is UTC−9 and Chukotka UTC+12, so Big Diomede is 21 hours ahead.
vo: between them runs the international date line. cross it, and the calendar jumps. big diomede is 21 hours ahead

claims.text: Big Diomede's civilian population was relocated to the Soviet mainland in 1948; only a border post and weather station remain.
vo: nobody lives on the russian side any more. its villagers were moved to the mainland in 1948, and today only a border post and a weather station remain

claims.text: About 80 people live in the village of Diomede on Little Diomede (83 in the 2020 census; 77 in 2023), which faces Russia.
vo: on the american side, about 80 people still live in the village, facing russia, facing tomorrow
